e.etymology: A surname meaning son of Hendry, a Scottish form of Henry, the Germanic name for a home ruler. It was in use as an American first name by the 1880s.
namesakes: Rickey Henderson (baseball's all-time stolen base leader)
Florence Henderson (Carol Brady on The Brady Bunch)

assoc.t: Henderson, Nevada, city beside Las Vegas

e.etymology: In Arabic a girls' name from hanan, compassion or tenderness. In Hebrew a boys' name, Hanan, gracious, from the same Semitic root as Hannah and John.
A phonetic spelling of Leah as it is said in Hebrew, LAY-ah, also used as a short form of Alayah. Leah is Jacob's first wife in Genesis.
A pet form of Gabrielle, Gabriella and Gabriela, feminine forms of Gabriel, from Hebrew for God is my strong man.
namesakes: Gabby Giffords (former congresswoman and gun-safety advocate)

assoc.t: Gabby of Gabby's Dollhouse, Netflix preschool series
gabby, an everyday word for talkative

e.etymology: A spelling of Rehan or Rayhan, from Arabic rayhan, sweet basil or fragrant herb, a word found in the Quran. The doubled-a spelling is common among Indian families.
A J spelling of Gianni, the Italian short form of Giovanni (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. In the US it is given to boys and girls about equally.
Brought into use by Jaden Smith, whose middle name is Syre and who titled his 2017 debut album Syre. Its earlier source is not documented.

assoc.t: Jaden Smith's 2017 album Syre

e.etymology: The English name of the wild cat, from Greek lynx, probably from a root meaning light, for the animal's shining eyes. As a first name it is a 2020s arrival beside Fox, Wolf and Bear.

assoc.t: the lynx, a tuft-eared wild cat
Minnesota Lynx, WNBA team
Lynx, a northern constellation

e.etymology: A compound of Anna, from Hebrew Hannah, grace, and Marie, the French form of Mary. Annemarie is the German and Dutch spelling.
A variant of Chase, an English surname for a huntsman, from Old French chacier, to hunt.
namesakes: Chace Crawford (actor in Gossip Girl and The Boys)

e.etymology: In Slavic countries, from Nike, the Greek goddess of victory, and a short form of Veronika. Nika is separately a Persian girls' name from nik, good, and a boys' short form in Georgia.

assoc.t: Sun God Nika in the manga and anime One Piece
Nika riots of 532 in Constantinople

e.etymology: A spelling of Ila that was most used in the US around 1900; its origin there is not recorded. Ila also exists as a Sanskrit name from Hindu tradition.
e.note: In Arabic, ilah is the word for a god or deity.

e.etymology: An English surname taken up as a girls' first name in the United States in the 2010s.
A respelling of Harmony, the English word used as a name, from Greek harmonia, a fitting together or agreement, also the name of a Greek goddess of concord.
From Latin Tiberius, of the Tiber, the river that runs through Rome. It was a common Roman first name and the name of the second emperor.

assoc.t: middle name of Star Trek's Captain James T. Kirk

e.etymology: A spelling of Arabic Isa, the name of Jesus in the Quran, where he is honored as a prophet.
From Sanskrit kavi, a poet or seer, the word used for the sages who composed the Vedic hymns.
A name of uncertain origin used mainly by Spanish speakers. It is popular in the Dominican Republic, where actress and TV host Nashla Bogaert carries it.
An English surname from the medieval women's name Diot, a pet form of Dionysia. As a first name it is chiefly American and peaked in 1953, the year Dwight D. Eisenhower became president.
namesakes: Dwight Schrute (Rainn Wilson's character on The Office)

assoc.t: Dwight Schrute of The Office
Dwight D. Eisenhower, thirty-fourth US president

e.etymology: From Polish Kazimierz, a Slavic royal and saint's name read as proclamation of peace. Several Polish kings bore it, and Saint Casimir is a patron of Poland and Lithuania.
namesakes: Casimir Pulaski (Polish cavalry general of the American Revolution)

assoc.t: Casimir effect in quantum physics

e.etymology: A given name usually of Italian origin, close to Gino, and sometimes a short form of Eugene or Eugenio.
The German, Scandinavian and Eastern European spelling of Victoria, from Latin victoria, victory, also the name of the Roman goddess of victory.
An English surname from a place name, Old English haes, brushwood, and tun, settlement.

assoc.t: actor Charlton Heston

e.etymology: An English occupational surname for a doorkeeper, from Old French ussier, from Latin ostium, door. The singer Usher Raymond IV made it familiar as a first name.

assoc.t: Usher, the R&B singer
usher, a person who shows people to their seats
The Fall of the House of Usher, Poe's story

e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Hayden, Hayley and Jaylen. Haylen also exists as a surname.
Most often a spelling of Arabic Rayyan, lush or well-watered, the name of the gate of Paradise reserved in Islamic tradition for those who fast.
A pet form of Olivia or Livia used as a full name. Livia is the feminine of Livius, a Roman family name; Olivia is tied to Latin oliva, olive.
A modern name modeled on Hawaiian names ending in -lani, sky or heaven, such as Leilani and Kailani.
A short form of Thomas in use since the Middle Ages and long given as a name in its own right. Thomas comes from Aramaic te'oma, twin.

assoc.t: Tom, the cat of Tom and Jerry
tom, a male cat or turkey
peeping Tom, a voyeur; Uncle Tom, a servile sellout

e.etymology: From Hebrew tal, dew, and Yah, a short form of God's name; Talia is the commoner spelling. Talya is also a short form of Natalia in some languages.

A respelling of Corbin, a surname from Old French corbin, little raven, once a nickname for someone dark-haired. This spelling is the one used by Korben Dallas, hero of the 1997 film The Fifth Element.
namesakes: Korben Dallas (Bruce Willis's hero in The Fifth Element)

assoc.t: Korben Dallas of The Fifth Element

e.etymology: A respelling of Elijah, from Hebrew Eliyahu, my God is Yahweh, the name of the Old Testament prophet who was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind.
